notes:
Summary: Mid-market B2B SaaS building an in-product conversational assistant + doc search. Currently on Hosted API trial; evaluating Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. Key asks: configurable VPC/Dedicated pool, EU residency for certain customer corp accounts, strong audit logs and KMS integration.

Technical constraints: wanting ~95-150 QPS for short messages (avg token length ~40), 99p latency target <120ms for chat in NA region, tail sensitivity, fallback for capacity spikes, KV cache for session state. Cost sensitivity: tight unit economics - target inference cost <$0.002 per 1k tokens for baseline prompts, looking to understand tradeoffs between batching, prefix caching, and INT8/4-bit quantization.

POC/Workshop outcomes: Redwood ran a cost workshop (03/05) covering:
- batching windows and dynamic micro-batching (pros/cons for latency)
- prefix/KV caching strategy to reduce repeated tokens for multi-turn flows
- suggested quantization profiles and expected throughput lift on T4/RTX-class GPUs
- unit-economics model (tokens -> $/request) that highlighted caching could cut per-session cost by ~40% for their dialogue patterns.

Quotes/voice: "If we can hit predictable cost per 1k tokens and keep 99p latency under 120ms, this is a go for Dedicated." — Head of Product, 03/05.
